<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which almost nothing happens, on purpose.</b><br>
  One young woman, one tall palm, one raft and a lot of time. She idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens: a bottle washes straight back, a delivery drone brings a spare pair of headphones, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and walks off wearing it. Every gag waits for the next bar of the music, so it lands on the beat.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p and 24 fps, always daytime. Every sound is synthesized from code.</sub>
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py        # live preview, and export to a YouTube-ready MP4
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>Program: CASTAWAY</b>: the tape, block by block</summary>

```text
 CASTAWAY                                          side A   counter 000
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  #  BLOCK                WHAT IS ON IT
  1  Program: CASTAWAY    the loader: python tools/serve.py, a web page
                          at http://127.0.0.1:8765/ with a live preview
                          and an export to MP4 (frame-exact, in the
                          browser; the server mixes in the sound)
  2  Bytes:   SCREEN$     6912 bytes: 6144 of picture, 768 of colour.
                          the island above. two colours per 8x8 cell
  3  Bytes:   SCHEDULE    activities.toml: more than 90 activities and
                          four timers, checked by python tools/schedule.py
  4  Bytes:   THEME       60 seconds, 80 BPM, F major, loops forever
  5  Bytes:   SFX         more than 150 sounds, none of them recorded
  6  Bytes:   VIDEO       10:00:00 at 24 fps: 864,000 frames
 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  duplicated by Leader Tone Duplicating. rewind fully before returning
```

At roughly 170 bytes a second, block 6 would bring in one 6912-byte frame every 41 seconds or so, and the whole video in a little over 13 months, as long as nobody touches the volume knob. The browser export manages 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p, so at that rate the same ten hours would take a bit over three. We consider that unsporting.

To run it the old way: <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>Symbol Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd>, <kbd>Symbol Shift</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd>, <kbd>Enter</kbd>, then press play on the tape. To run it the new way: `python tools/serve.py`.

<sub>Leader Tone Duplicating is made up. So is the tape.</sub>

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SCHEDULE</b>: four timers and a great deal of calm</summary>

Everything she does lives in [`activities.toml`](activities.toml): more than 90 activities (94 on 2 October 2026, and the list grows every few hours), each on one of four timers or chained after another one.

```text
 TIMER         COMES ROUND EVERY     IN A TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN
 regular       2 to 5 minutes        about 155
 occasional    12 to 25 minutes      about 30
 rare          30 to 60 minutes      about 13
 super rare    3 to 6 hours          about 2  (never more than 3)
 chained       only after another    the tide after a sandcastle
```

"Typical" is the median of 200 simulated runs. She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut, and every activity starts on the next bar of the music (every 3 seconds), which is why the screen above loops every 8 bars. The default run is `10:00:00` with seed `1992`; `python tools/schedule.py` checks the file and simulates one.

A short tour of the gags: the message in a bottle that washes straight back (a different bottle brings a reply, later); the delivery drone whose parcel is another pair of headphones; the sea turtle who visits; the grey tabby who arrives on a crate, climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats off again; the hunt for signal (one bar, top of the palm); the shark in headphones who nods to the beat; the tour boat of selfie-takers; the bro on an electric hydrofoil who throws a shaka and carves off; the kumara she plants, which grows over the video; and the very rare day she walks out over the water and comes back with an iced coffee. She could leave any time.

Around her, 26 bits of scene life: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; birds, planes with vapour trails, whales, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SOUND</b>: made by code, heard by nobody (yet)</summary>

Every sound comes out of [`tools/make_audio.py`](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far.

```text
 THEME     60-second seamless loop, 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi
           20 bars of exactly 3 seconds
           electric piano, kalimba lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle
 OCEAN     60-second seamless loop
 MIX       -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP
 LEVELS    a master for each kind of sound, and one per routine
```

Nobody has listened to any of it yet, so we will not tell you it sounds lovely. The meters are happy, though.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>HOW THIS SCREEN LOADS</b>: the rules it keeps</summary>

The banner is one SVG, drawn by a small Node script with no packages, and it keeps the rules of an early-80s 8-bit home computer, because the rules are the look:

- **256 by 192 pixels, cut into 32 by 24 cells, two colours per cell.** One INK, one PAPER and one BRIGHT bit for the pair. Where the palm meets the sea the frond tips go a darker green, because the cell they share with the water is not BRIGHT. That is not shading. That is the rules.
- **The picture loads in memory order.** Three thirds, top to bottom; inside each third, the top pixel line of all eight text rows, then the second line, and so on, so it fills like a venetian blind. The colour comes last, one row of cells at a time.
- **The border is the tape.** Thick red and cyan bands for the pilot tone, thin blue and yellow stripes for data, where a 1 bit is twice as thick as a 0 bit. The stripes here are the real bits of the word CASTAWAY.
- **It waits for the bar.** The loop is 24 seconds, which is 8 bars of the theme at 80 BPM, and every phase starts on a bar line. Once loaded, her head, the shark and the music note keep the beat (0.75 seconds), and the bottom lines change every bar.

The font, the logo letters and the island are drawn from scratch in the generator; nothing is lifted from a real machine or a real game. With reduced motion on, it skips the loading and shows the finished screen. The stripes are slowed right down and only roll while it loads.

</details>
